Before South Africa diamonds were rare because at that time they only existed in river beds. Prices were high and pretty much they were only held by the ruling class.  

When diamonds began to be mined on an industrial scale, their supply far outweighed demand. Prices dropped and they were at risk of being yet another semi-precious stone. Rather than trying to compete on price, Cecil Rhodes (De Beers founder), bought out all mining competitors to then artificially restrict supply. That strategy worked for a few hundred years until science found a way to manufacture artificial diamonds which are virtually indistinguishable from those that come from the ground.

Interesting pattern with compute I keep seeing.  

So NVIDIA just used 8k GPUs to simulate a quantum computer that doesn't exist yet.  

The pattern is chips built for a specialized usecase solving problems better then general compute, and almost all one of them still needs GPUs to work.  

Everyone's heard of the inference chips, Groq, Etched, Cerebras, plus the hyperscalers' own, TPUs, Trainium, Maia.  As well as the large labs adding chips built for fast inference, but they still train their models on GPUs.
